#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Real Claude Code across several repos on one machine with global tracking on:
# a repo enabled BEFORE the tier, one enabled AFTER, un-enabled (globally
# tracked), excluded, vetoed (enabled:false), and no repo at all.
# Real HOME (real claude auth + real user-level hooks calling `entire` via PATH),
# sandboxed ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR, dev binary first on PATH.
set -u
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
T="$S/real3"; rm -rf "$T"; mkdir -p "$T/config" "$T/bin" "$T/srv/acme"
ln -sf "$S/entire-bin" "$T/bin/entire"
export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH" ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR="$T/config" ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 ENTIRE_LOG_LEVEL=debug
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$T/gitconfig"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.name "Test User"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" user.email "test@example.com"
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" commit.gpgsign false
git config --file "$GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL" init.defaultBranch main
echo "binary: $(command -v entire) ($(entire version 2>/dev/null | head -1))"
PORT=9420
git daemon --reuseaddr --base-path="$T/srv" --export-all --enable=receive-pack --port=$PORT --detach --pid-file="$T/daemon.pid"
sleep 1
trap 'kill $(cat "$T/daemon.pid") 2>/dev/null' EXIT

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  ✓ $1"; }
bad()  { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  ✗ $1"; }
check(){ if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1"; fi; }
info() { echo "  · $1"; }
section(){ echo; echo "=== $1"; }
claude_run() { # claude_run <outfile> <args...>
  local out="$1"; shift
  env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format json "$@" > "$out" 2> "$out.err" < /dev/null
  echo "    claude: rc=$? $(jq -r '"session=\(.session_id) cost=$\(.total_cost_usd) error=\(.is_error) → \(.result|.[:80])"' "$out" 2>/dev/null)"
  grep -v 'no stdin data' "$out.err" | sed 's/^/    claude stderr| /'
}
mkrepo() { # mkrepo <dir> <bare-name>
  git init -q --bare "$T/srv/acme/$2.git"
  git init -q "$1"; ( cd "$1" && git remote add origin git://localhost:$PORT/acme/$2.git && echo "# $2" > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -q -m init && git push -q -u origin main )
}
hooklog() { ls "$1"/.entire/logs/*.log "$1"/.git/entire/worktree/*/logs/*.log 2>/dev/null | head -1; }
hookcount() { grep -c "\"hook\":\"$2\"" "$(hooklog "$1")" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- E1: enabled BEFORE the tier
section "E1 repo enabled BEFORE global tracking turned on"
E1="$T/e1"; mkrepo "$E1" e1; cd "$E1"
entire enable --agent claude-code 2>&1 | grep -E 'Trusted|Installed|Configured' | sed 's/^/    enable| /'
git add -A . && git commit -q -m "enable entire" && git push -q origin main
check "no user settings yet → no trust recorded" "! test -s $T/config/settings.json"

section "turn the tier on (user settings), then work in E1"
echo '{"global":{"enabled":true}}' > "$T/config/settings.json"
entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "E1 status: Enabled (repo-level)"      "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '● Enabled'"
check "E1 activation_source=local"          "entire status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -e '.global_tracking.activation_source==\"local\"'"
check "E1 untrusted (explicit enable predates the tier)" "entire status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -e '.global_tracking.trust_state==\"untrusted\"'"
claude_run "$T/e1.json" "Create e1.txt containing the line 'e1'. Do not run git commands."
check "E1 metadata in worktree .entire/ (local layout)" "ls -d .entire/metadata/*"
check "E1 no runtime root under .git (local layout)"   "! ls -d .git/entire/worktree/*/ 2>/dev/null | grep -q ."
info "hook invocations this session: user-prompt-submit=$(hookcount "$E1" user-prompt-submit) stop=$(hookcount "$E1" stop) session-start=$(hookcount "$E1" session-start)"
check "repo-level + user-level hooks did not double-fire" "test $(hookcount "$E1" user-prompt-submit) -eq 1 && test $(hookcount "$E1" stop) -eq 1"
check "no WARN/ERROR in E1 hook log"        "! grep -qE '\"level\":\"(WARN|ERROR)\"' $(hooklog "$E1")"
grep -E '"level":"(WARN|ERROR)"' "$(hooklog "$E1")" | cut -c1-240 | sed 's/^/    log| /'
git add e1.txt && git commit -q -m "e1" && git push origin main 2>"$T/e1.push"; grep -v '^To \|main -> main' "$T/e1.push" | sed 's/^/    push| /'
check "E1 held (tier on, not yet trusted)"  "grep -q 'checkpoint sync held' $T/e1.push"
entire trust 2>&1 | grep -v '^Warning: global' | sed 's/^/    trust| /'
echo "" >> README.md; git commit -q -am t; git push origin main 2>"$T/e1.push2"; grep -v '^To \|main -> main' "$T/e1.push2" | sed 's/^/    push| /'
check "E1 checkpoints on remote after trust" "git ls-remote origin | grep -q entire/checkpoints"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- E2: enabled AFTER the tier
section "E2 repo enabled AFTER global tracking is on → trust recorded by enable"
E2="$T/e2"; mkrepo "$E2" e2; cd "$E2"
entire enable --agent claude-code 2>&1 | grep -E 'Trusted|Configured' | sed 's/^/    enable| /'
check "enable recorded trust for e2"        "jq -e '.global.trusted_origins|index(\"localhost/acme/e2\")' $T/config/settings.json"
git add -A . && git commit -q -m "enable entire" && git push -q origin main 2>/dev/null
claude_run "$T/e2.json" "Create e2.txt containing the line 'e2'. Do not run git commands."
git add e2.txt && git commit -q -m "e2" && git push origin main 2>"$T/e2.push"; grep -v '^To \|main -> main' "$T/e2.push" | sed 's/^/    push| /'
check "E2 synced on first push (no hold)"   "! grep -q 'held' $T/e2.push && git ls-remote origin | grep -q entire/checkpoints"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- G1: never enabled
section "G1 never-enabled repo → tracked globally"
G1="$T/g1"; mkrepo "$G1" g1; cd "$G1"
claude_run "$T/g1.json" "Create g1.txt containing the line 'g1'. Do not run git commands."
check "G1 header Tracked globally"          "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '● Tracked globally'"
check "G1 runtime root under .git"          "ls -d .git/entire/worktree/*/metadata"
check "G1 worktree clean except g1.txt"     "test \"\$(git status --porcelain)\" = '?? g1.txt'"
check "G1 hooks fired exactly once each"    "test $(hookcount "$G1" user-prompt-submit) -eq 1 && test $(hookcount "$G1" stop) -eq 1"
git add g1.txt && git commit -q -m g1 && git push origin main 2>"$T/g1.push"
check "G1 held until trusted"               "grep -q 'checkpoint sync held' $T/g1.push"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- X1: excluded
section "X1 excluded via exclude_paths → nothing captured"
X1="$T/x1"; mkrepo "$X1" x1
jq --arg p "$X1" '.global.exclude_paths=[$p]' "$T/config/settings.json" > "$T/tmp.json" && mv "$T/tmp.json" "$T/config/settings.json"
cd "$X1"; entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "X1 inactive_reason=repo_excluded"    "entire status --json 2>/dev/null | jq -e '.global_tracking.inactive_reason==\"repo_excluded\"'"
claude_run "$T/x1.json" "Create x1.txt containing the line 'x1'. Do not run git commands."
check "X1 no session state"                 "! ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json"
check "X1 no runtime root, no git hooks"    "! test -d .git/entire && ! test -f .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg"
git add x1.txt && git commit -q -m x1 && git push origin main 2>"$T/x1.push"
check "X1 push has no Entire output"        "! grep -qi entire $T/x1.push"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- V1: vetoed
section "V1 committed .entire/settings.json {enabled:false} → veto"
V1="$T/v1"; mkrepo "$V1" v1; cd "$V1"
mkdir -p .entire && echo '{"enabled": false}' > .entire/settings.json && git add .entire && git commit -q -m veto
entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "V1 status Disabled + inactive here"  "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '○ Disabled' && entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -qi 'inactive here'"
claude_run "$T/v1.json" "Create v1.txt containing the line 'v1'. Do not run git commands."
check "V1 no session state"                 "! ls .git/entire-sessions/*.json"
check "V1 no runtime root"                  "! test -d .git/entire"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- N1: no repo
section "N1 Claude launched outside any git repository"
N1="$T/norepo"; mkdir -p "$N1"; cd "$N1"
entire status 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    status| /'
check "status outside a repo shows the global line" "entire status 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'global tracking: on'"
claude_run "$T/n1.json" "Create n1.txt containing the line 'n1'."
check "claude ran fine"                     "jq -e '.is_error==false' $T/n1.json"
check "no entire errors on stderr"          "! grep -i 'entire' $T/n1.json.err | grep -qiE 'error|fatal|panic'"
check "nothing written here"                "! test -d .entire && ! test -d .git"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- cross-repo (informational)
section "cross-repo turn: cwd=G1, edits a file inside E2 (binding is a separate trail — informational)"
cd "$G1"
claude_run "$T/x.json" "Write the single line 'from g1' into the file $E2/cross.txt using the Write tool. Do not run git commands."
info "E2 has cross.txt: $(test -f $E2/cross.txt && echo yes || echo no)"
info "G1 sessions: $(ls $G1/.git/entire-sessions/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')   E2 sessions: $(ls $E2/.git/entire-sessions/*.json 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
info "G1 pending: $(entire checkpoint list --pending 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'session updates')"

echo; echo "==================== $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ===================="
echo "test root: $T"

# Security review — `feat/global-trust` (global tracking tier)

Scope: non-test Go files in the branch diff vs `origin/main`, traced from repo-controlled inputs (committed `.entire/*`, submodules, symlinks, `core.hooksPath`, remote URLs) to file writes, argv, activation, and egress decisions. Two findings clear the confidence bar; both share one root cause.

---

## Finding 1 — Repo-shipped `.entire/settings.json` is treated as the user's own repo-level enablement: activates capture in excluded repos, runs full setup (git-hook install + worktree writes) from user-level hooks

- **Where:** `cmd/entire/cli/settings/repopolicy/policy.go:36-51` (activation precedence), `repopolicy/activation.go:50-80` (`ReadRepoActivation` — project file = "configured", default enabled), `repopolicy/types.go:106-111` (`RuntimeRoot` → `<worktree>/.entire` for `ActivationLocal`), `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/global_setup.go:196-213` (`EnsureSetupForHook` → `ensureSetup` when repo-configured), `strategy/common.go:316-337` (`ensureSetup`: `EnsureEntireGitignore`, `EnsurePrimaryRefTo`, `installGitHooks`), `cmd/entire/cli/hook_registry.go` (`executeAgentHook` → `prepareHookPolicy`), `cmd/entire/cli/root.go:147-150` (comment acknowledging the pin-out).
- **Severity:** Medium (High when combined with Finding 2)
- **Category:** consent/exclusion bypass; unintended writes in a never-enabled repo
- **Confidence:** 0.8

**Description.** With `global.enabled=true`, Entire's hooks fire in every repo via `~/.claude/settings.json` / `~/.gemini/settings.json`. `ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` consults the repository's own `.entire/settings.json` *first*; a project file with any content (or `enabled` absent) yields `Configured && Enabled` → `ActivationLocal`, and in that branch `exclude_paths`, `exclude_paths_exact` and `exclude_origins` are never evaluated (they live only in `ClassifyGlobalConfig`, reached from the `default:` case). On main, a committed `.entire/settings.json` was inert until the user ran `entire enable` (or accepted Claude Code's project-hooks trust prompt); on this branch a bare clone is sufficient. The code treats "repository ships `.entire/settings.json`" as indistinguishable from "this user ran `entire enable` here", but the former is attacker/third-party content.

Consequences for such a repo, all without any user action beyond opening an agent session in it:
1. Capture is active even when the worktree matches the user's `exclude_paths`/`exclude_origins` (the branch's own guarantee for excluded repos is bypassed by repo content).
2. `EnsureSetupForHook` takes the *repo-configured* route (`RepoActivationConfigured` = true) and runs the full `ensureSetup` — it installs Entire's git hooks into the repo's hooks dir **without** the `HooksDirIsWorktreeResident` guard that the global route applies, writes `.entire/.gitignore` via plain `os.ReadFile`/`os.WriteFile` (`common.go:1423-1474`, follows a repo-committed symlink), and runtime files (`.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}`) are written under the literal worktree `.entire/` — a directory the hostile repo controls, including any symlinks it committed there. (The checkpoint walkers do skip symlinked entries, so this is a write-through, not a read-through — see "not exploitable" below.)
3. Egress: under `trust_all` (offered as a first-class option in the pre-push prompt and warned about as "captured AND synced"), `DecideEgress` returns Allowed for this repo, so transcripts from an *excluded* repo are pushed to that repo's sync remote on the user's next `git push`.

**Exploit scenario.** User has `global.enabled=true`, `exclude_paths: ["~/clients/**"]`, `trust_all: true`. They clone a third-party repo into `~/clients/acme/` that carries a committed `.entire/settings.json` (this is the normal way teams share Entire settings, so it is not suspicious). They open Claude Code there. TurnStart → `prepareHookPolicy` → `ActivationLocal` (exclusion never consulted) → `ensureSetup` installs `.git/hooks/pre-push` etc. and creates `.entire/.gitignore`, `.entire/metadata/…`, `.entire/logs/…` in the clone. On the next `git push`, `CheckpointEgressAllowed` is true (trust_all) and the session transcript leaves the machine to acme's remote, contrary to the user's exclusion.

**Fix.** Treat repo-shipped settings as *configuration*, not *consent*: (a) apply the user's exclude lists to `ActivationLocal` as well (an exclusion is the user's explicit "never here" and should outrank repo content), or at minimum apply them whenever the global tier is enabled; (b) record repo-level enablement in a machine-local place the repo cannot ship (e.g. the clone-preferences file in the git common dir, written by `entire enable`) and require that, not merely the presence of `.entire/settings.json`, before taking the `ensureSetup`/worktree-layout route from a hook; repos that only have committed settings would then go through the invisible global route (git-common-dir runtime root, hooks-dir residency check, trust prompt). (c) Have `status`/the SessionStart banner say when a repo is active *because of committed settings* rather than a local enable.

---

## Finding 2 — Local-layer ownership probe is defeated by a submodule mounted at `.entire`, letting a clone deliver `.entire/settings.local.json` that is honored as the developer's own — including the exec-bearing OPF `command`

- **Where:** `cmd/entire/cli/settings/opf_command_trust.go:284-353` (`probeLocalSettingsIsVersioned`: symlink check at 289-305, index scan 322-330, HEAD scan 337-352), `:401-431` (`treeHasPathFold` — `continue` on `object.ErrDirectoryNotFound`), `settings.go:637-660` (`loadMergedSettings` merges the local layer unless `localTracked`; `enforceOPFCommandTrust` requires `localOwn`), `repopolicy/activation.go:32-39,55` (`LocalSettingsTrusted` uses the same probe), `settings.go:1628-1636` (`CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` → bypasses `checkpointRemoteIsInherited` in `checkpoint/remote/util.go:412`), `redact/opf.go:421-426` (`exec.CommandContext(callCtx, s.command, …)`), `strategy/manual_commit_push.go:251-286` (pre-push OPF run).
- **Severity:** High
- **Category:** exec of repo-controlled command; consent-gate bypass
- **Confidence:** 0.8

**Description.** The gate that decides whether `.entire/settings.local.json` is "this developer's own" is: not a symlink at `.entire` or the file (new on this branch), not present in the superproject index, and (deep) not present in HEAD. A repository that declares a **submodule at path `.entire`** defeats all three: after `git clone --recurse-submodules` (or `git submodule update --init`, which most READMEs instruct), `<root>/.entire` is a real directory containing whatever the attacker's submodule holds; the superproject index/HEAD contain only a gitlink entry `.entire` (mode `0160000`), so `pathsEqualFold(".entire", ".entire/settings.local.json")` is false, and in the HEAD walk `tree.Tree(".entire")` hits go-git's `GetTree` → `ErrObjectNotFound`, which go-git v6 maps to `ErrDirectoryNotFound` (`plumbing/object/tree.go:119-131`), so `treeHasPathFold` `continue`s and returns `(false, nil)`. Both shallow and deep probes therefore report `localOwn`. Effects:

1. `loadMergedSettings` merges the attacker's local layer (so `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.{enabled,prompt_default,categories,command}` all take effect) and `enforceOPFCommandTrust` keeps `command` because `localSetsOPFCommand` is true and the deep probe says `localOwn`.
2. `ReadRepoActivation` honors the local `enabled` key; `CheckpointRemoteIsLocalOnly` returns true, so a `checkpoint_remote` in that file skips the owner-mismatch ("inherited") check.
3. At pre-push, after the egress gate passes, `redact.OPFEnabled()` → `resolveOPFDecisionForPrePush` (`prompt_default: "always"` skips the prompt; non-TTY auto-runs) → `RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF` → `exec.CommandContext(ctx, command, "--device", …)` with the hook's cwd at the worktree root. A `command` such as `./.entire/opf` (a script shipped in the same submodule) executes on the developer's machine.

The probe's index/HEAD logic itself predates this branch, but on main the chain was unreachable without the user running `entire enable` in the hostile repo. This branch makes the repo active from a bare clone (Finding 1), installs the pre-push hook from the agent hook, and added a symlink guard specifically for "a clone can ship the file without the literal path appearing in the index" — the gitlink shape is the same class and is not covered.

**Exploit scenario.** Attacker publishes a repo with `.gitmodules` mapping path `.entire` to a second attacker repo containing `settings.json` (`{}`), `settings.local.json` (`{"redaction":{"openai_privacy_filter":{"enabled":true,"prompt_default":"always","command":"./.entire/opf"}}}`), and an executable `opf`. Victim (global tracking on) runs `git clone --recurse-submodules …`, opens Claude Code in it (capture starts; `ensureSetup` installs `.git/hooks/pre-push`), and later pushes anything. If `trust_all` is set the egress gate passes immediately; otherwise the victim sees the one-time prompt "Yes — sync this repo's checkpoints to origin (…)" — a natural "yes" for someone pushing their own branch. `pendingCheckpoints > 0` (the session was captured), OPF is enabled by the local layer, no prompt (`always`), and `./.entire/opf` runs as the victim with the victim's environment. Without `trust_all` the same path also needs a TTY-less push (GUI client) or the OPF prompt default; both are attacker-set.

**Fix.** In `probeLocalSettingsIsVersioned`, treat a gitlink at any component of `.entire/settings.local.json` as *versioned/hostile*: while scanning the index, also match entries whose `Name` equals a proper prefix of the target path (`.entire`) — any such entry (file or `filemode.Submodule`) means the path is repository content; in `treeHasPathFold`, if a fold-matching entry has `Mode == filemode.Submodule` (or `Tree()` fails for a non-blob entry), return `true` rather than `continue`. Independently, `enforceOPFCommandTrust` should refuse `command` values that resolve inside the worktree (relative paths, or absolute paths under the worktree root), since an executable delivered by the repository is exactly what the gate exists to block — that closes the exec even if some future delivery shape slips past the ownership probe. Consider also making the OPF `enabled`/`prompt_default` keys committed-or-local-verified in the same way `command` is, since they are what make the exec run unattended.

---

## Examined and judged not exploitable (with guarding code)

1. **Symlink-following writes into user config** (`jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicFollowingSymlinks`, `resolveWriteTarget`, `write.go:86-159`). Only reached with user-owned paths: `~/.config/entire/settings.json` (`user_settings.go:114`), `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.gemini/settings.json` (`claudecode/hooks.go:335,486`, gemini equivalent). No repo-derived path reaches it — repo-side `.entire/settings.local.json` writes use the non-following `WriteFileAtomic` (`settings.go:776`), which replaces rather than follows a link. Hop cap (40) and `seen` map prevent cycles; the final-component walk only follows links the user placed. TOCTOU would require local write access to `$HOME`, out of scope.

2. **Global-route runtime path routing** (`paths/invisible.go:55-80`, `repopolicy/repository.go:64-75`). For `ActivationGlobal` the runtime root is `<git-common-dir>/entire/worktree/<sha256(worktreeID)[:16]>`; `commonDir` comes from `git rev-parse` and is symlink-canonicalized; `runtimeRootForPath` fails closed with `ErrUnroutableRuntimePath` on any policy error or a `WorktreeRoot` mismatch, and every consumer (`lifecycle.go`, `state.go`, opencode/pi lifecycle) skips rather than falling back to a worktree path. Lazy hook install checks `HooksDirIsWorktreeResident` (`global_setup.go:122-157`, symlink-resolved on all sides) so a committed `core.hooksPath` target never receives hook files on that route. The checkpoint walkers (`ephemeral.go:964-980`, `persistent.go:2440-2455`) `Lstat` every entry and skip symlinks, so a hostile `.entire/metadata` symlink cannot pull foreign files into a checkpoint.

3. **Trust-key / exclusion normalization** (`gitremote.ParseURL`, `splitOwnerRepo`, `repopolicy.NormalizeOrigin`, `CanonicalTrustOrigin`). With `trust_all`, transcripts are then pushed to that repo's remote on the next `git push` with no banner or prompt. Not RCE (the hooks installed are Entire's own), so not High; but it defeats a documented, explicit user consent control and the repo-content threat model the codebase already applies to `settings.local.json`.

## Evidence

**Leg 1 — repo-shipped project file activates an excluded repo (holds)**

**Leg 2 — setup writes + git-hook install from a hook in a never-enabled clone (holds)**

- `hook_registry.go:109-131`: hook proceeds whenever `policy.Active`.

## Mitigations found (and why they don't close it)

- SessionStart banner "Entire is capturing this repo locally…" (`lifecycle.go:294-306`) fires only when egress is **held** (`CheckpointEgressHeld`), so a `trust_all` user gets no indication at all.

In `ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` (`policy.go`), when `userSettings.GlobalEnabled()` and activation comes from the **project** file (not an untracked, user-authored `settings.local.json` with `enabled: true`, which is the user's own action and should keep overriding), evaluate the exclusion lists before granting `ActivationLocal`; on a match return inactive with `InactiveReasonGlobalExcluded`. This keeps the `enabled:false` veto and `entire enable --local` semantics intact and makes exclusion symmetric with the existing veto. ## Security review — `feat/global-trust` (PR #2030, now at `21c3daa5a`)

Two findings survived discovery **and** independent false-positive filtering (both 8/10). Both are fixed, verified, pushed. This is what actually raised the monitor, not the vague "new parsing surfaces" summary.

# Vuln 1: Consent/exclusion bypass via repo-shipped `.entire/settings.json` — `repopolicy/policy.go:43-51`

* Severity: **Medium** (confidence 8/10)
* Description: `ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` consulted the repo's own `settings.json` first and evaluated `exclude_paths` / `exclude_paths_exact` / `exclude_origins` only on the global branch. With the tier on, user-level hooks fire in every repo, so any clone carrying a committed `.entire/settings.json` (even `{}`) activated capture inside a folder the user had excluded, installed Entire's git hooks there from an agent hook (without the hooksPath-residency guard), wrote `.entire/{metadata,logs,tmp}` into the clone, and under `trust_all` synced its transcripts on the next push with no banner. The codebase already rejects a shipped `settings.local.json` for exactly this reason — the project file carried identical power without the check.
* Exploit scenario: user has `exclude_paths: ["~/clients/**"]`, `trust_all: true`; clones a third-party repo that ships `.entire/settings.json` (the normal way teams share settings) into `~/clients/acme`; opens Claude Code there → captured, hooks installed, transcript pushed to acme's remote on next push.
* Fix (shipped): `ExcludedByGlobalConfig` is shared by both activation branches; while the tier is on, exclusions outrank a committed `settings.json`. Only an untracked `settings.local.json` with an explicit `enabled` key (`RepoActivation.LocalOverride` — the developer's own action) still activates an excluded repo. Test: `TestPrepareHookPolicy_CommittedProjectFileCannotBypassExclusions`; real-Claude scenario X2.

# Vuln 2: OPF `command` exec via submodule mounted at `.entire` — `settings/opf_command_trust.go:294-330, 415-419`

* Severity: **High** (confidence 8/10)
* Description: the "is `settings.local.json` this developer's own?" probe checked symlinks, exact index paths, and HEAD trees. A **submodule at `.entire`** defeats all three: `git clone --recurse-submodules` yields a real directory (symlink check passes); the superproject records only a gitlink named `.entire` (never the file's path); and go-git maps the gitlink's missing tree object to `ErrDirectoryNotFound`, which `treeHasPathFold` read as "not tracked". The shipped local file was honored as the developer's own — including `redaction.openai_privacy_filter.command: "./.entire/opf"`, exec'd at pre-push with cwd at the worktree root (`exec.ErrDot` doesn't apply to a command containing a separator). Pre-existing probe gap, but newly reachable from a bare clone on this branch (hooks auto-install; the only human decision left is the checkpoint-sync prompt, which never mentions executing anything).
* Fix (shipped): probe treats an index entry *named* `.entire` (any mode), a `filemode.Submodule` entry in HEAD, and an `.entire/.git` on disk as versioned; `enforceOPFCommandTrust` additionally rejects any command resolving inside the worktree, regardless of ownership. Tests: `TestOPFCommandTrust_SubmoduleAtEntireDirIsIgnored` (index+HEAD), `TestOPFCommandTrust_CommandInsideWorktreeIsRejected`, integration `…UntrackedLocalCommandInsideWorktreeIsNotExecuted`; the positive integration test now installs its shim outside the repo.

Examined and not exploitable: symlink-following user-config writes (only user-owned paths reach it), global-route runtime path routing (fail-closed, walkers skip symlinks), trust-key/exclusion URL normalization quirks (collapse to same repo or fail-closed), committed `checkpoint_remote` (owner-mismatch guard), cmd.exe rule (no new dynamic argv).

## Verification (all on the final binary)

- `mise run check`: lint 0, **88 pkgs ok / 0 FAIL**, canary 56/56 + 4/4, exit 0.
- Scripted user suite **50/50**; real Claude single-repo **34/34**; real Claude multi-repo **33/33** — enabled-before/after tier, globally tracked, excluded, **excluded + committed settings (new)**, vetoed, no-repo, hook dedup.
- Pushed `f7f1665da..21c3daa5a`, checkpoint `01M1549RE4VB535YCZ5WGWP5S8`, PR head `21c3daa5a`.

## Still open for your decision

1. **Committed `settings.json` as consent for hook install / worktree writes in a *non-excluded* clone.** The validator rated leg 2 real but I left the "committed settings activate a fresh clone" rule intact — the docs call it deliberate and changing it (e.g. requiring a machine-local `enable` record, or routing such repos through the invisible global path) alters team-repo behavior. Your call.
2. **No banner for `trust_all` users** — the SessionStart "capturing this repo" banner only fires when egress is *held*, so under `trust_all` a new repo is captured and synced silently. Cheap to add; say if you want it.
3. Trail 1074's third finding (`resolveWriteTarget`) remains incorrect and should be dismissed; the two on my code were fixed in `f7f1665da`.
4. Cross-repo attribution = trail 1018 (unmerged, 2 conflicts vs this branch) — pending your pick of the three options from earlier.

1. if it alters team repo behavior, then this seems like no right? do we normally commit the settings.jsom? 
2. yes, add banner
3. dismiss then
4. i forget the three options from earlier, but to run the successful actual global enable test, do we need to pull this too, to test how I want because right now it seems the tests we're doing are nto working? so makes me think the global enable does not work

content.text:
All four items closed or answered. PR #2030 head is now `0fdc6da45`.

## 1. Committed `settings.json` — leave it, yes

You're right. `.entire/settings.json` is committed by design: this repo tracks its own, `entire enable` writes it as the "team-shared" file, and the docs tell teams to commit it. Making a committed file stop activating a clone would break every team's normal setup. The exclusion fix that shipped (`21c3daa5a`) is the right mitigation: a shipped `settings.json` can no longer override your `exclude_*` lists, but a repo you or your team enabled still just works. No further change.

## 2. Banner — done (`0fdc6da45`)

A globally tracked repo whose checkpoints sync only because `trust_all` is on now gets a SessionStart banner naming `trust_all`, the settings file, and `exclude_paths` as the opt-out. Per-repo consent and repo-enabled repos stay quiet. Verified through the real hook path in the sandbox; full check green (lint 0, 88 pkgs ok, canary 56/56 + 4/4).

## 3. Dismiss — needs one click from you

The API lets me post on threads but rejects every resolve/dismiss field shape, so I posted the reasoning on both `resolveWriteTarget` threads (the reviewer re-flagged the same incorrect claim on the new head, so there are two) and "fixed in `f7f1665da`" notes on the two threads about my code. Dismissing/resolving is a UI action on trail 1074 — four open threads, all annotated.

## 4. Does global enable work? Yes — the tests are not failing

I want to be precise here because I think my earlier informational output caused the doubt. Everything global enable is *specified* to do passed with **real Claude Code sessions, on the final binary**: 34/34 single-repo (fresh repo, resume, commit/hold/trust/drain, bare-path origin, fork consent) and 33/33 multi-repo (repo enabled before the tier, enabled after, never enabled, excluded, excluded-with-committed-settings, vetoed, no repo, hook dedup). Nothing in those runs failed.

The one thing that "didn't work" was my cross-repo probe: **one Claude session, launched in repo G1, writing a file into repo E2** — the file landed, but E2's commit got no session link. That isn't global enable breaking; it's a feature global enable never had: attributing a *single session* to *multiple repos*. That's trail **1018 / PR #1959 (`feat/session-binding`)** — "binding = automatic adopt, checkpoint every touched repository" — deliberately split out and **not on this branch**.

So the answer to "do we need to pull this too?": **only if the scenario you want to test is one session spanning repos** (e.g. Claude launched from a parent folder, or told to edit a sibling repo). If your scenario is "Claude in repo A that isn't enabled, and separately in repo B that is" — that's covered and passing today.

The three options, restated:
1. **Merge `feat/session-binding` into this branch now** — 16 commits, +3.9k lines, 2 conflicts (`hook_registry.go`, `settings/settings.go`), 245 commits behind main. Lets us run the cross-repo test for real on the combined code, at the cost of a much bigger PR #2030.
2. **Build a throwaway integration worktree** (this branch + 1018 merged, not pushed to #2030), run the real cross-repo scenario there, and decide afterwards whether 1018 stacks on #2030 or merges on its own. My recommendation — you get the test you want without committing to the PR shape.
3. **Ship #2030 as is**, cross-repo as the follow-up it was planned to be.

Say which and I'll proceed.

The exclusion fix that shipped (21c3daa5a) is the right mitigation: a shipped settings.json - does this contradict or is new infra that what exists with the .entire/settings.json that is comitted by ream members or we're just talking about the same thign right?

Same file, same convention — no new infra and no contradiction. Let me lay it out plainly.

**What stays exactly as it is:** teams commit `.entire/settings.json`; anyone who clones the repo has Entire active there. That was true on `main`, it's true on this branch, and `21c3daa5a` did not touch it.

**What the fix adds is one narrow exception, on the developer's own machine:** if *that developer* has turned global tracking on **and** listed this repo (by path or origin) in *their own* `~/.config/entire/settings.json` exclude lists, then the repo is inactive for them — even though the team's committed `settings.json` says "enabled".

| Situation | main | this branch before fix | after fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Team repo with committed `settings.json`, developer has no user-level exclusions | active | active | **active** (unchanged) |
| Same repo, developer excluded it in their user settings | *(exclusions don't exist on main)* | active — committed file overrode the personal exclusion | **inactive** — the developer's exclusion wins |
| Developer ran `entire enable --local` themselves in an excluded folder (untracked `settings.local.json`) | active | active | **active** (their own action) |

So the only behavior that changed is the middle row, and it changed in the direction a developer would expect: something *they* wrote in *their own* config outranks something that arrived by `git clone`. That was already the rule for a shipped `settings.local.json` on this branch; the fix just applies the same rule to the shipped `settings.json`.

Why this matters security-wise is the case the review found: without it, *any* repo you cloned that happened to contain a `.entire/settings.json` (even `{}`) would be captured, get hooks installed, and under `trust_all` have its transcripts synced — regardless of your exclusions. With it, your exclusions are actually authoritative. For teams that don't use exclusions, nothing is different.
but shouldnt that then be in their local config then?

Both places exist today and they cover different scopes — the fix didn't move anything between them, it made one of them work consistently.

**Per-repo opt-out → `.entire/settings.local.json`** (in the clone, gitignored). A developer who doesn't want Entire in one team repo writes `{"enabled": false}` there — that's the "local veto wins over project" rule, it's what `entire disable` writes in a repo-enabled repo, and it's unchanged. If that's the case you have in mind: yes, that belongs in local config, and it already lives there.

**Machine-wide patterns → `~/.config/entire/settings.json` exclude lists.** These exist for the global tier and express things a per-clone file can't: "never track anything under `~/clients/**`", "never track `github.com/acme/private-*`". They apply to repos you haven't cloned yet and to hundreds of clones at once, without visiting each one to plant a veto file — that's the whole point of a pattern.

The bug was that the second mechanism silently didn't apply to the repos most likely to exist on a real machine: team repos, which ship a committed `settings.json`. So a developer who wrote `exclude_paths: ["~/clients/**"]` would still have every client repo captured (and hooks installed, and under `trust_all` synced), and the only way to actually get the exclusion they'd asked for was to fall back to per-clone vetoes in every clone — which is the thing the pattern was meant to save them from. The fix makes the user's own exclude list mean what it says. It adds no new config surface.

Put differently: local config is where you say "not *this* repo"; user config is where you say "not *these kinds of* repos". Before the fix only the first statement was reliable; now both are.
and is this consistent in codebase?

Mostly, because every hook and command decides "is this repo active?" through one classifier (`repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy`), so the fix lands everywhere at once — but let me verify that claim against the code rather than assert it, and check the one place I suspect drifts: `status`, which reads `settings.Load().Enabled` directly for its header.

Short answer: the *behavior* was already consistent — one classifier decides — but the *display* wasn't, and I found and fixed that gap while checking.

**How I checked.** I grepped every place that decides "is this repo active / enabled" and mapped it against the classifier:

- **Consistent (13 call sites → `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy`):** agent hooks (`hook_registry`, `hook_policy`), git hooks (`hooks_git_cmd`), pre-push gates (`manual_commit_push`), lazy setup (`global_setup`), runtime path routing (`paths/invisible`), `trust`, `doctor`, `enable`'s trust recording, root post-run, and `status`'s global-tracking line. Because exclusions now live inside that one classifier, the fix applied to all of them at once — the real-Claude X2 run proved it: excluded repo with a committed `settings.json` → no session state, no hooks, no writes, silent push.
- **Two places read raw repo settings directly** (`RepoActivationConfigured`): `EnsureSetupForHook` — only reachable after the classifier said active, so fine — and `entire disable`'s "is there repo-level setup?" routing, which is about config presence, not activation. Fine.
- **The inconsistency: `entire status`.** Its header came from `settings.Load().Enabled`, not the classifier. For X2 it printed `● Enabled · branch main` / `Checkpoints sync to: origin` two lines above `global tracking: on (this repo is excluded)`, and `--json` said `enabled: true` next to `active_here: false`. Two sources of truth on one screen. Same root cause would have hit anyone reading `status --json` to decide if Entire is on.

**Fixed in `9b917c6a7`** (pushed; PR head): `status` now sides with the classifier — `○ Excluded on this machine · branch main` + the reason and the user settings path, no sync lines, `enabled: false` / `repo_excluded` in JSON. And the mirror-image trap: `entire enable` inside an excluded folder still writes the repo-level setup but now says why global tracking keeps it inactive and points at `entire enable --local` (this clone's own untracked file, which does override). Verified live in the sandbox; `E1` (enabled, not excluded) unchanged; full check green (lint 0, 88 pkgs ok, canary 56/56 + 4/4).

So today's model is uniform: **per-repo opt-out** = `settings.local.json` (`enabled:false`, or `enable --local` to opt *in* past an exclusion); **machine-wide patterns** = user file exclude lists; committed `settings.json` = team default that everything else can override — and every surface (hooks, gates, status, doctor, trust, enable) reports the same answer.

PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok()   { PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  ✓ $1"; }
bad()  { FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  ✗ $1"; }
check(){ if eval "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1"; fi; }
info() { echo "  · $1"; }
section(){ echo; echo "=== $1"; }
claude_run() { local out="$1"; shift
  env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT claude -p --model haiku --permission-mode acceptEdits --output-format json "$@" > "$out" 2> "$out.err" < /dev/null
  echo "    claude: rc=$? $(jq -r '"session=\(.session_id) cost=$\(.total_cost_usd) error=\(.is_error) → \(.result|.[:90])"' "$out" 2>/dev/null)"

content.text:
Verified end to end — and this time the cross-repo scenario works, on the merged code plus one small integration fix.

## Findings dismissed
The API turned out to accept a JSON body (`--input {"resolved": true}`); all four open threads on trail 1074 are now resolved: the two incorrect `resolveWriteTarget` claims (with the reasoning posted), and the two on my code (with "fixed in `f7f1665da`" notes). **0 open threads.**

## Both branches pulled together: `test/global-plus-binding`
Worktree `~/dev/…/cli/.worktrees/global-plus-binding` = `feat/global-trust` @ `9b917c6a7` + `origin/feat/session-binding` merged (2 conflicts resolved: binding's early payload read + no-repo evidence kept alongside the policy gate and session-start notice in `hook_registry.go`; `IsSetUpAtRoot` kept alongside `RepoActivationConfigured` in `settings.go`). Builds; cli tests pass. Not pushed.

## Real `claude -p` across repos — E repo-enabled, G never enabled (global), tier on

**First run (merge as-is): 13/17.** One-directional:
- launched in G, edits E → E adopted the session, both commits linked ✓
- launched in E (or a parent dir), edits G → **G never adopted, G's commits orphaned** ✗

Cause: session-binding decides "is this repo enabled?" with `IsSetUpAtRoot` — *do `.entire/settings*.json` files exist* — the exact question global tracking makes obsolete (a globally tracked repo has no settings files by design).

**Integration fix (one commit on the test branch):** new `settings.IsActiveAtRoot(ctx, root)` → `repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicyAt(root).Active`, used at binding's two decision points (`binding_tap.go` evidence, `binding_adopt.go` re-check). Exclusions and vetoes come along for free.

**Second run: 17/17.**

| Session launched in | edits | E (enabled) | G (global) |
|---|---|---|---|
| G | E + G | adopted, commit linked | own, commit linked |
| E | E + G | own, commit linked | **adopted, commit linked** |
| parent dir (no repo) | E + G | adopted, commit linked | adopted, commit linked |

Each of G's three checkpoints lists only G's file (`from-s1/2/3.txt`) with the shared transcript; G's worktree stays byte-clean with runtime under `.git/entire/worktree/…`; both remotes received their checkpoints on push. So: **global enable works, and combined with 1018 + that one fix, a single session spanning an enabled repo and a never-enabled repo is attributed to both.**

## What this means for the PRs
- **#2030 (`feat/global-trust`)** is complete and verified on its own; head `9b917c6a7`.
- **1018 (`feat/session-binding`)** needs the `IsActiveAtRoot` change to compose with global tracking, plus a rebase (245 behind main) and its own review threads. One more integration caveat I noticed but didn't hit: the trust-identity election is cwd-scoped, so a *foreign* repo's egress decision inside a binding hook would read the source repo's election — adoption only needs `Active`, so it didn't matter here, but a real merge should make that resolver root-aware.

Your call on shape: (a) push `test/global-plus-binding` as a stacked PR on #2030, or (b) carry `IsActiveAtRoot` + the rebase over to PR #1959 and land 1018 after #2030. I'd do (b) — it keeps #2030's review scope what it is and lands the merge-order conflicts once.
yes we'll do b, but should we fix the cause of failure for the first run and then what made the second run successful

Yes — and the two are the same thing: the cause of the first-run failure was binding asking "are there `.entire/settings*.json` files here?" (`IsSetUpAtRoot`), and what made the second run pass was replacing that with "does the policy classifier say this repo is active?" (`IsActiveAtRoot`). That fix is what should land, but it can't go into PR #1959 as it stands: 1018 is based on `main`, which has no `repopolicy`/global tier — `IsActiveAtRoot` only exists once #2030 has merged.

So for (b) I'd split it:
1. **#2030 gets the seam now** — `settings.IsActiveAtRoot(ctx, root)` plus an activation-only classifier variant (no egress decision), so asking about a *foreign* repo never runs the cwd-scoped trust/election code for the wrong repo (that closes the caveat I flagged too). Tested here against globally-tracked / excluded / vetoed / repo-enabled roots from a different cwd.
2. **1018's rebase after #2030 lands** — only the two call-site changes in `binding_tap.go` / `binding_adopt.go`, plus the cross-repo test.

Implementing step 1 in the #2030 worktree now. Reading the classifier to add the activation-only variant cleanly.

Done — the seam is on #2030 (head `077a2e3dd`), and the cause/fix pair is now split cleanly across the two PRs as planned for option (b).

## What the first run's failure was, and what fixed it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Cause** | Session-binding decided "is this repo enabled?" by file presence — `IsSetUpAtRoot` = *does `.entire/settings*.json` exist there?* Global tracking's whole point is that a tracked repo has **no** settings files, so every globally tracked repo silently fell out of cross-repo attribution (S2/S3: E adopted, G never did). |
| **Fix** | Ask the policy classifier instead: `settings.IsActiveAtRoot(ctx, root)` → `repopolicy.ClassifyActivationAt(root)`. Same precedence as everything else (repo settings → tier → exclusions/vetoes), for an explicit root. With that at binding's two decision points, all three launch shapes attributed to both repos (17/17). |

## What landed where

**#2030 — `077a2e3dd` (pushed, full check green: lint 0, 88 pkgs ok, canary 56/56 + 4/4):**
- `repopolicy.ClassifyActivationAt` — activation-only variant. Deliberately **no egress decision**: the sync-remote election is cwd-scoped, so deciding trust for a foreign root would read the wrong repo's remotes. This also closes the caveat I flagged earlier.
- `ClassifyRepoPolicyAt` = that + egress (behavior unchanged; veto path still returns before trust as before).
- `settings.IsActiveAtRoot` for foreign-repo callers.
- Test `TestClassifyActivationAt_ForeignRootFromAnotherCwd`: classifies the *given* root from a different cwd — globally tracked → active/global with Trust untouched; excluded → inactive; vetoed → inactive; repo-enabled → local. Doc section "Asking about another repository".

**1018 (PR #1959) — after #2030 merges and it rebases:** two one-line call-site changes (`binding_tap.go:197` evidence `Enabled:`, `binding_adopt.go:35` re-check) from `settings.IsSetUpAtRoot(root)` → `settings.IsActiveAtRoot(ctx, root)`, plus the cross-repo test. The reference implementation is sitting on the local branch `test/global-plus-binding` (merge + that fix, 17/17 verified); I haven't pushed it. Say if you want it pushed as a reference branch, or a comment on #1959 describing the change — otherwise I'll leave it local until the rebase.

Trail 1074: 0 open threads. Auth context is still `github:peyton-alt@us.auth.entire.io`.
so did you add to ask another question, or can you tell me the fix more simply please

Simply:

**The problem:** the session-binding code (1018) checks whether a repo is "Entire-enabled" by looking for `.entire/settings.json` on disk. Globally tracked repos don't have that file — that's the whole idea of global tracking — so binding thought they weren't enabled and never attached the session to them.

**The fix:** make binding ask the same question everything else asks — "is Entire active in this repo?" — using the policy classifier, which knows about global tracking, exclusions, and vetoes. One new helper, `settings.IsActiveAtRoot(ctx, root)`, and binding calls it instead of checking for the file.

**Where it lives:**
- The helper is on **#2030** now (just pushed), because it depends on the global-tracking code that only exists on this branch.
- The two lines in binding that switch to the helper go into **#1959** once it rebases on top of #2030 — they can't compile before that.

No new question added. The only outstanding "ask" was a minor one: whether you want the reference branch pushed. Default: I'll leave it local and apply the two lines when 1018 rebases.
Globally tracked repos don't have that file - is this wrong behavior?

No — that's the intended design, and one of the core promises of global tracking.

**Why globally tracked repos have no `.entire/settings.json`:**

- `.entire/settings.json` is the **team's** file — committed, shared, "Entire is on for this project." Global tracking is a **personal, machine-level** choice: "capture my agent sessions everywhere on *my* machine." Writing a team file into every repo you touch would either show up as an untracked file in someone else's project or, if committed, turn Entire on for the whole team without their consent.
- The feature's stated invariant is **zero worktree footprint**: `git status --porcelain` stays byte-clean; runtime data (`metadata`, `logs`, `tmp`) lives under `.git/entire/worktree/<hash>/`; the only thing Entire writes into `.git` is runtime data and a stamp. That's what the "invisible" branch of the feature stack was about, and every test today verifies it (`git status` shows only the user's own file).

So the absence of the file is correct. What was wrong was **binding's assumption** — written before global tracking existed — that "no settings file" means "Entire isn't here." That assumption was true on `main` and stopped being true on this branch. The fix updates the assumption (ask the classifier), not the layout.
how si that teams file when every individaul has settings.json when entire is enabled, like right now, if i enable entire in two repos, are two settings.jsons files created in both repos?

Yes — `entire enable` writes one `.entire/settings.json` **per repo**, in that repo's own working tree. Enable in two repos → two files, one in each. There's no single file shared across repos.

"Team file" doesn't mean "one file for the team" — it means *the copy in each repo is shared with everyone who works on that repo*, because it's version-controlled. Three scopes, all different files:

| File | Lives in | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|
| `.entire/settings.json` | each repo's worktree | everyone who clones that repo (committed) — the "team" copy |
| `.entire/settings.local.json` | each repo's worktree | only you, only this clone (gitignored) |
| `~/.config/entire/settings.json` | your home dir | only you, every repo on this machine (global tracking, exclusions, trust) |

So when you `entire enable` in your own repo and commit, you're deciding *for that project*: anyone who clones it gets Entire on. When a repo is globally tracked instead, you've decided only *for your machine*, and nothing is written into the project — which is why no `settings.json` appears there.
shoudl this be part of the lazy install then too that this file gets written in teh repos? and we can warn about it too?

I'd recommend against it. Writing `.entire/settings.json` lazily would undo the property global tracking is built on, and it solves a problem we've already solved a better way.

**Why not:**

1. **Wrong scope.** `settings.json` is the project's decision, shared with everyone who clones. Global tracking is your machine's decision. Writing the team file as a side effect of a personal setting means: you open Claude in a repo, a new untracked `.entire/` appears, and the moment anyone `git add -A`s it, Entire is turned on for the whole team — without them choosing it. That's the consent problem from the security review, just pointed the other way.
2. **It ends "invisible".** Every repo you touch would grow an untracked directory; `git status` is no longer clean in projects you don't own. The runtime layout would also flip to the worktree (`.entire/metadata`, `logs`) because a repo with `settings.json` is classified as repo-enabled. A gitignored `settings.local.json` doesn't help — that's still a file in someone else's tree, and the `.gitignore` that hides it lives inside `.entire/` too.
3. **It would re-create the weakness we just closed.** "A settings file exists" is exactly the signal a hostile clone could plant, and exactly the signal binding wrongly relied on. The fix was to stop deriving activation from file presence and ask the classifier — writing the file to satisfy file-based checks goes backwards.
4. **A warning doesn't fix the side effect.** You can warn once, but the file is still there and still committable.

**What already covers the visibility need:** `entire status` says `● Tracked globally`; the SessionStart banner fires when sync is held or `trust_all` is on; `doctor` reports the tier; and `entire enable` is the explicit step for "I want this to be a project-level, team-shared decision" — that's the right moment to write the file, because a person chose it.

If the concern is that a developer might not *realize* a repo is being captured, the lighter option is a one-time SessionStart notice in a globally tracked repo ("Entire is capturing this repo via global tracking; run `entire enable` to make it project-level, or add it to `exclude_paths`"). That informs without writing into the project. Want that?
so what was your solution to the problem then beacuse this file is not in all the rpeos? it seemsl ike it will become a roblem

Fair challenge. Let me answer it and then check the codebase for anything else that could trip on it.

**The solution isn't "put the file everywhere" — it's "nothing is allowed to ask whether the file exists."** Every decision about whether Entire is active in a repo goes through one classifier (`repopolicy.ClassifyRepoPolicy`), which knows a repo can be active with no file at all (global tier), inactive with a file present (excluded, vetoed), and so on. Binding was the one piece of code still asking the old question, because it was written on `main` before global tracking existed. Fixing it meant pointing it at the classifier, not planting files.

Whether it "becomes a problem" depends on whether any *other* code asks the old question, or new code does later. Let me check that concretely, and see if we can make it structural (a lint rule) rather than a convention.
